reviewMethods: Read AGENTS.md first; two clean complete rounds for this user-authorized release supersede the repository default three.
Independently read deployment implementation, CLI/install/account/HTTPS and recovery transitions, pinned build/runtime, root/native/gateway ownership, operation publication and workspace helpers.
Read all scripts, CI jobs, tooling tests, root documentation and deployment guide; inspect command examples and compatibility/rollback qualifications.

Parse every scoped Python file and enumerate all 366 test cases, assertions, platform skips and external/privileged boundaries. Manually review critical account/HTTPS/recovery fixtures; cross-check remaining fixture coverage against implementation.

Parse all historical feature-evidence JSON; validate source references, count and method relationships, read claims and limits. Preserve stale source-hash evidence as historical, never as a current test result.
Check lockfile and package/workspace pins offline, without dependency installation or network calls.
No prior audit conclusion used to establish correctness. Parent-reported findings outside this scope are not classified by this report.
focusedBoundaryReview: Single admin bootstrap salted scrypt/hash-only publication, root/gateway permissions, password input handling and recovery pending semantics.
Account login verification through loopback with declared origin, cookie handling, proof recheck and invalid password/redirect/error rejection.
Built-in HTTPS account prerequisites, strict legacy ownership, transaction backup/restore, removal of old identity service only after account verification.
Application and control authentication downgrade guards; failed legacy-to-account upgrade remains stopped and repair --target candidate revalidates the retained account release.
Pinned runtime/dependency staging and isolated build boundaries; root-owned release manifests and bounded no-link archive/export behavior.
Management requests and journals preserve delivery uncertainty, exact identity and recovery barriers.
Workspace paths, data/index backup recovery, Git lock publication, acknowledgement/witness authority and retained managed worktrees.
Full-test gate remains default-three unless a separate concrete explicit authorization record applies; skipped/incomplete tests are not full passes.
CI selection, stable report completeness, isolated native environment and fail-closed result handling.
